trials.claimQuote:
### Unlimited Plan: $19 (was $588)
- Lifetime access to Feedbeo
- You must redeem your code(s) within 60 days of purchase
- All future plan updates
trials.reasoning: The binding terms allow the vendor to suspend an account or disable access for extended inactivity and other reasons, materially limiting unconditional lifetime access.

exhibits.quote: We may suspend your user account or temporarily disable access to whole or part of any Service in the event of any suspected illegal activity, extended periods of inactivity or requests by law enforcement or other government agencies.
exhibits.argument: Lifetime access can be suspended or disabled by the vendor for inactivity or other reasons.

exhibits.quote: I've bought a lifetime licence following the instructions to activate.
exhibits.argument: Buyer reports lifetime licence activation did not happen despite following instructions.

exhibits.quote: I'm a speaker and the ROI for a lifetime deal is hard to beat.
exhibits.argument: Buyer explicitly references a lifetime deal with positive ROI, supporting lifetime access.

trials.claim: Unlimited links, admin seats, participants and polls
trials.claimQuote:
- Unlimited links (hashtag #codes)
- Unlimited admin seats
- Unlimited participants
- Unlimited polls
- Data export & analytics
trials.reasoning: A buyer states unlimited admin seats, an advertised part of this claim, still do not exist, despite defense evidence for unlimited participants and polls.

exhibits.quote: This means that the following advertised premium features still do not exist: Unlimited Admin Seats, Data Exports/Analytics, and Branding.
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms advertised unlimited admin seats do not actually exist after purchase.

exhibits.quote: When you add an admin, you cannot delete them.
exhibits.argument: Admin seat management is broken because added admins cannot be removed.

exhibits.quote: Whether you have the free or the paid plan, there's no limit to the number of participants who can join an event, so you can engage with your entire audience, no matter how big or small.
exhibits.argument: Vendor states there is no limit to participants on free or paid plans.

exhibits.quote: Feedbeo shines when it comes to live engagement: unlimited polls, Q&A, and word clouds all update smoothly, and presenters pick it up within minutes.
exhibits.argument: Buyer confirms unlimited polls work smoothly in live engagement.

trials.claimQuote:
- All future plan updates
- Please note: This deal is not stackable
- Unlimited links (hashtag #codes)
- Unlimited admin seats
trials.reasoning: The exhibits only show the vendor can modify terms and some features are not yet available; neither directly proves or disproves that future plan updates are included.

exhibits.quote: We may modify the Terms upon notice to you at any time through a service announcement or by sending email to your primary email address.
exhibits.argument: Vendor reserves right to modify terms at any time, undermining guaranteed future updates.

exhibits.quote: There are features mentioned which are not avaiable yet; but the developers are working on them.
exhibits.argument: Advertised features are admitted to be unavailable and only promised for the future.

trials.claimQuote:
### Unlimited Plan: $19 (was $588)
- Lifetime access to Feedbeo
- You must redeem your code(s) within 60 days of purchase
trials.reasoning: The regular $39/mo website price is not evidence deal buyers are charged that price, and no exhibit verifies the $19 versus $588 deal pricing.

exhibits.quote: From time to time, we may change the price of any Service or charge for use of Services that are currently available free of charge.
exhibits.argument: Vendor can change prices at any time, undermining the claimed $19 versus $588 value.

exhibits.quote: Interestingly, the Unlimited (Business) plan is advertised for $39/mo on the product website, but I am confused why it is listed for purchase when its premium features are still not available.
exhibits.argument: Official site prices the plan at $39 per month, making the $588 comparison misleading.
